crops.name: Rice (Basmati transplanted)
crops.notes: Days counted from transplanting (nursery ~30 days not included). Puddling + ponding: land-prep and seepage/percolation terms are explicit assumptions.
crops.verification: Calendar from Punjab Agriculture Dept guidance (basmati transplanting July); Kc FAO-56 Table 12; salinity FAO-29 (Maas & Hoffman); percolation is an assumption - VERIFY LOCALLY

crops.name: Wheat
crops.notes: Terminal heat during grain filling (Mar-Apr) is the key climate risk in Punjab plains.
crops.verification: Calendar from Punjab Agriculture Dept (irrigated sowing Nov 1-30); Kc FAO-56; heat threshold from wheat heat-stress literature (~32 C); salinity FAO-29

crops.name: Maize (autumn hybrid)
crops.notes: Sensitive to standing water in early growth and to heat at silking.
crops.verification: Calendar from Punjab autumn maize guidance (late Jul - mid Aug); Kc FAO-56; salinity FAO-29

crops.name: Mungbean (summer short-duration)
crops.notes: Fits the post-wheat fallow window. Biological N fixation; heat >40 C at flowering causes flower drop.
crops.verification: Window inferred from wheat harvest + rice transplanting gap (Punjab rice-wheat mungbean insertion); Kc FAO-56 (beans/mung); salinity FAO-29; heat threshold from legume literature - VERIFY LOCALLY

crops.name: Cotton (Bt)
crops.notes: Long season: picking can run into wheat sowing window (late wheat risk).
crops.verification: Calendar from Punjab Agriculture Dept cotton sowing (Apr-May); Kc FAO-56; salinity FAO-29

rotations.name: Rice → Wheat
rotations.description: The existing dominant system in the Punjab rice-wheat zone.

rotations.name: Rice → Wheat → Mungbean
rotations.description: Adds a short-duration legume in the summer fallow between wheat harvest and rice transplanting.

rotations.name: Maize → Wheat
rotations.description: Replaces puddled rice with autumn maize before wheat.

rotations.name: Cotton → Wheat
rotations.description: The dominant system of the southern Punjab cotton zone.

rotations.name: Maize → Wheat → Mungbean
rotations.description: Maize-wheat with a summer legume in the fallow window.

traits.forage_use: rice straw (pual) is a poor-quality dry fodder
traits.pest_notes: Grass host. Rice followed by wheat (both grasses) favours the grassy weed Phalaris minor (dumbi sitti) in wheat and carries over some soil-borne diseases.
traits.soil_notes: Puddling breaks soil structure and forms a plough pan that limits the roots of the next crop. Burning the straw removes organic matter.
traits.source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept and PARC rice-wheat system guidance

traits.forage_use: wheat straw (bhusa) is the main dry fodder for livestock in Punjab
traits.pest_notes: Grass host. Shares grassy weeds and some soil-borne diseases with rice and maize.
traits.soil_notes: Deep fibrous roots and stubble protect the soil from December to April.
traits.source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept

traits.forage_use: green fodder and silage; stover after grain harvest
traits.pest_notes: Grass host but not flooded: replacing rice removes the flooded conditions that rice pests and puddling need. Watch fall armyworm.
traits.soil_notes: Deep roots can loosen a plough pan left by puddled rice. Large stover adds organic matter if not burned.
traits.source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept and PARC maize guidance

traits.forage_use: haulm and leaves are fed to livestock after picking
traits.main_pests: whitefly (yellow mosaic virus); thrips; pod borer
traits.pest_notes: Not a host of most cereal pests and diseases: it breaks the grass-on-grass cycle. Shares whitefly with cotton.
traits.soil_notes: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen with root bacteria. A 60-70 day crop that covers the soil in the hot April-June fallow. Leaves and roots add nitrogen and organic matter.
traits.source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); NARC and AARI pulses guidance

traits.forage_use: little on-farm fodder; cottonseed cake is a purchased feed
traits.main_pests: pink bollworm; whitefly (cotton leaf curl virus); jassid
traits.pest_notes: Not a grass: breaks cereal pest and grassy weed cycles. Shares whitefly with mungbean.
traits.soil_notes: Deep taproot reaches subsoil water and loosens compacted layers. Few residues stay on the field.
traits.source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Central Cotton Research Institute Multan guidance
